source.note: FIRST asserted-ABSENCE gold (ADR-0004 §1, the pattern Appendix B sketches). The claim under review is NOT 'this line is unparseable' — it parses cleanly — but 'a deck-construction ability can never be a party to any in-game flow, so no flow arm can ever follow from it'. Oracle text verified byte-exact against Data/_01_Raw/Datasets/External/oracle-cards.json (name='Rat Colony', mana_cost='{1}{B}', type_line='Creature — Rat'): 'This creature gets +1/+0 for each other Rat you control.\nA deck can have any number of cards named Rat Colony.' edhrec_rank is null in the testbed source — popularity omitted (not fabricated). AST faithful, not a wish: the committed parser gold Fixtures/HandParsedCards/RatColony.json parses line 1 to a StaticAbility with a single Effect { EffectType: anyNumberInDeck } (no target, no quantity, no subject — the effect carries no payload at all, which is itself the tell). LIVE PROJECTION VERIFIED (PortWalk over that gold, 2026-07-20): Rat Colony projects exactly two ports, emit 'modify:pt' and emit 'emit:anynumberindeck', BOTH with a null PortStructure — the coarse totality fallback (PortGraph.EmitPort's `{ } other => emit:{other}` arm), no IPortFamily recognizes either. anyNumberInDeck is on the known-coarse-projections.json whitelist today with the prose reason 'baseline coarse fallback (initiative-03 inception 2026-06-15) — no flow rule consumes it yet'. That prose is exactly the drifting derived claim ADR-0004 §1 exists to dissolve: it says 'not yet', implying backlog, when the truth is TERMINAL BY THE RULES. This gold replaces the sentence with an executable assertion. CR grounding: 'A deck can have any number of cards named Rat Colony' is a static ability (CR 604.1 — 'static abilities do something all the time … they're simply true') that modifies the rules for deck construction, and CR 113.6n rules that such an ability FUNCTIONS BEFORE THE GAME BEGINS: it lifts the CR 100.2a four-of limit ('a constructed deck may contain … no more than four of any card with a particular English name other than basic land cards') during deck construction, and does nothing whatsoever once a game has started. There is no zone it functions in, no event it raises, no store it moves, and no continuous in-game value it produces (CR 604.2's continuous effects are 'active as long as the permanent … remains on the battlefield … or … in the appropriate zone, as described in rule 113.6' — for this ability that zone-set is empty, because the whole game is after its window closed). So the terminality is not a gap in the taxonomy waiting to be filled by a future stem: NO in-game consume can exist for it, because the ability has already finished functioning before any consume could observe anything. NEAR-MISS THE JUDGE PINNED (and why the stem is scoped to the CR 113.6n class specifically, not to 'functions outside the game'): COMPANION (CR 702.139) also functions before the game begins, yet carries an in-game special action (CR 116.2g — 'pay {3} and put that card into your hand'), so 'functions before the game begins' is NOT a synonym for 'terminal'. What makes THIS ability terminal is that it modifies the deck-construction RULES and grants nothing else; companion/wish/sideboard effects must not be folded into this stem. Corpus sweep of the 13 cards whose text modifies deck construction (Rat Colony, Relentless Rats, Shadowborn Apostle, Persistent Petitioners, Dragon's Approach, Hare Apparent, Slime Against Humanity, Templar Knight, Tempest Hawk, Seven Dwarves, Nazgul, ...): in every one the deck-construction sentence is a standalone line and the in-game text ('count Rats', 'count Slimes in your graveyard') is a SEPARATE ability with its own ports — no printed card reads another card's deck-construction ability in game, and CR 113.6n gives it no in-game window in which it could. Contrast this with the OTHER known-coarse entries: attach (CR 701.3) is NOT terminal in this sense and is deliberately not the subject of this gold — the 2026-07-18 investigation recorded in known-coarse-projections.json concludes attach is blocked on a missing BecomesAttached trigger event that real printed cards say verbatim ('Whenever this Equipment becomes attached to a creature' — Assimilation Aegis; 'As this Equipment becomes attached to a creature' — Psychic Paper; both verified against oracle-cards.json), i.e. it is genuine BACKLOG, not a decision. ADR-0004 Appendix B uses attach as its worked example; this gold deliberately does not. The interaction-judge (2026-07-20) confirmed Appendix B's premise — 'attaching emits no event a trigger subscribes to' — is FALSE per CR 603.2, so Appendix B should be re-worked to this gold or annotated illustrative-only; it also corrected the investigation note's own cite of CR 701.3d for 'becomes attached' (701.3d defines becoming UNattached; no CR subrule defines becoming attached as an event, which is itself corroborating evidence that the modeling gap is real and event-shaped). Both flagged for the ADR owner. ADR-3 canonical: side=emit, kind=BEHAVIOR (a static ability, CR 604.1 — ADR-0003 §1 places statics in BEHAVIOR; note this ability has no CR 604.2 in-game continuous effect at all, since 604.2 scopes such an effect to the CR 113.6 zone-set and here that set is empty — the kind follows from 'it is a static', not from an in-game continuous effect), stem='deck-construction' (a new top-level stem, no supergroup: the §4 supergroups are all in-game event/state families and none of them would be honest for an out-of-game rules modification), attrs {} (no facet: the ability has no payload, no target, no duration, and no quantity — 'any number' is the REMOVAL of a limit, not a quantity the ability carries). structured=false records that the live engine deliberately produces no PortStructure for it, which is what distinguishes intentional terminality from an unconverted family (ADR-0004 §2's backlog subtrahend: an unserved projection with no gold is backlog; one with an asserted-absence gold is a decision). Rat Colony's OTHER ability (the +1/+0-per-other-Rat static, which the live engine projects as the coarse unstructured 'modify:pt' emit) is deliberately NOT declared here — this gold witnesses one thing, following the kari-zev-skyship-raider precedent of partial port declaration; declaring it would drag a novel 'delta' axis value into the rollup for no witnessing purpose.

judge.ref: interaction-judge 2026-07-20 — PASS: deck-construction terminality is CR-correct (113.6n functions before the game begins; 100.2a is the lifted limit; 604.1 static), no printed counterexample in corpus (companion CR 702.139 is a distinct class, not 113.6n); falsification prompt answered — assertion catches an arm added on stem `deck-construction` but NOT one added on the engine's live coarse label `anynumberindeck`, so the gold must carry a second no_arm probe on that label; PROCEED. AMENDED the same day per that required correction: the port records coarse_label='emit:anynumberindeck', the runner probes BOTH spellings and asserts the label is still projected unstructured, closing the judge's CONCERN; its two prose nits (604.2 cited for the kind; the omitted second port called modification:creature when the live label is modify:pt) are corrected above.

Rat Colony.note: THE WITNESS (of an ABSENCE) — 'A deck can have any number of cards named Rat Colony.' A static ability (CR 604.1 — hence BEHAVIOR by ADR-0003 §1, which places statics there) modifying the deck-construction rules, which per CR 113.6n functions BEFORE THE GAME BEGINS and lifts the CR 100.2a four-of limit. It has NO CR 604.2 in-game continuous effect (604.2 scopes a static's continuous effect to the CR 113.6 zone-set, and here that set is empty) — that absence IS the terminality. AST-derivable from StaticAbility.Effects[0] = { EffectType: anyNumberInDeck } — an effect with no target, payload, quantity or duration. STEM SCOPE (judge-required pin): stem='deck-construction' means the CR 113.6n class SPECIFICALLY — an ability that modifies the deck-construction RULES and does nothing else. It is NOT the broader 'functions outside the game' class: companion (CR 702.139) also functions before the game begins yet carries an in-game special action (CR 116.2g), so companion/wish/sideboard effects must NOT be folded into this stem. Deliberately carries no PortStructure (structured=false): the live PortWalk projects the coarse label 'emit:anynumberindeck' with a null Structure via PortGraph.EmitPort's totality fallback, and no stem in the ADR-0003 §4 root would be honest for an out-of-game rules modification. coarse_label records that live spelling so the assertion is executed over BOTH vocabularies, and so the gold goes red if a family ever starts structuring the label (see no_arm[P0]).

assertions.because: For every consume probe in the current universe — every stem the rollup witnesses, plus every consume PortStructure the engine's own families project over the hand-parsed card corpus (facets and all) — PortFlowMatcher.SelectArm(P0, consume) returns null. This is asserted against the MATCHER, never against a materialized edge set: a single-card gold has no partner card, so 'zero edges' would be vacuously true and would keep passing after somebody armed the port. Sibling of the established no_loop claim. Evaluated against the CURRENT taxonomy, so it strengthens as stems accrete; if a future change arms this port, THIS GOLD GOES RED (a hard build failure), forcing the judgment to be re-derived rather than silently outliving its premise. TWO SPELLINGS ARE PROBED (interaction-judge 2026-07-20 required correction): the canonical ADR-0003 stem 'deck-construction' AND the engine's live coarse label 'emit:anynumberindeck' (per coarse_label), because the realistic wrong-making change is somebody writing an IPortFamily for the LATTER — a probe on the canonical stem alone would sail past it. The runner additionally checks that the coarse label is still projected UNSTRUCTURED over the corpus, so the gold goes red the moment a family starts recognizing it, before any arm exists. The CR justification for expecting it never to go red: the ability has finished functioning before the game begins (CR 113.6n) and grants no in-game action (unlike companion, CR 702.139/116.2g), so no in-game consume — present or future — can observe anything it does.

P0 projects the BEHAVIOR stem deck-construction (a static ability's continuous modification of the deck-construction rules, CR 604.1/604.2/113.6n). A new top-level stem with no supergroup parent — the §4 supergroups are in-game event/state families, none of which would be honest for an out-of-game rules modification. The rollup will mark it unpredicted:true (the scaffold never declared it), which is correct: it is not a capability hole being burned down, it is a terminal leaf being recorded so the derived backlog can subtract it.

Intentional structural terminality, not an unconverted family. Verified against the live engine: PortWalk projects 'emit:anynumberindeck' with a null PortStructure via the coarse totality fallback. This is what removes anyNumberInDeck from the derived backlog (projected − served − asserted-unarmable, ADR-0004 §2); without this gold it would correctly appear as unserved demand. Not yet executable (structural-claim grammar); the executable half is no_arm[P0].
unit=single-card: a port derivation witnessing a terminal stem, no cycle closed and no edge (edges=[]) — and by the no_arm claim above, no cycle CAN be closed through this port.
